subject.title: [Bug] web_fetch fails in dual-stack networks when DNS returns IPv6 special-use addresses

question: Should `web_fetch` default DNS-result validation filter blocked answers and proceed when at least one safe public address remains, or keep the current reject-any-blocked DNS policy?
rationale: The code fix is small, but it changes the default SSRF interpretation for hostile or polluted DNS answers; automation should not choose that security boundary without owner intent.

options.title: Filter blocked answers by default
options.body: Land a narrow fix that pins only allowed addresses, rejects all-blocked result sets, and adds mixed IPv4/IPv6 regression coverage.

options.title: Keep strict reject-any-blocked behavior
options.body: Leave the current security posture in place and document that affected deployments must use trusted proxy or explicit fake-IP config where applicable.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in mode
options.body: Preserve the current default and add a named configuration switch for mixed-answer tolerance, with migration-free docs and tests.

recommendation.title: Filter blocked answers by default
recommendation.body: Land a narrow fix that pins only allowed addresses, rejects all-blocked result sets, and adds mixed IPv4/IPv6 regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The current helper and several recent SSRF refactors/docs changes trace to this account, making it the strongest routing candidate for the default security-policy choice.
